svg.text: GPU Kernel DSL + MLIR Compiler - TTIR - TTGIR - LLVM - triton-lang.org
L3 - TTIR Triton Dialect (tt.* - hardware-agnostic tile IR)
tt.ptr<T> - block pointers - no layout yet
L4 - TTGIR TritonGPU Dialect (ttg.* - layout-encoded distributed tensors)
Encoding maps (thread_id, reg_idx) to tensor element - drives coalescing + comm patterns
L5 - TTGIR Optimization Passes (layout + matmul + memory + pipeline)
L6 - Backend Lowering (TTGIR - LLVM IR - PTX/AMDGCN - CUBIN/HSACO)
Python kernel - MLIR stages - GPU binary - cached launch
Step 1: @triton.jit Python AST - semantic analysis - TTIR (tt.* MLIR)
Step 2: TritonToTritonGPU - attach layout encodings - TTGIR (ttg.*)
Step 3: TTGIR opt passes - layout propagate - matmul accel - pipeline loops
Step 4: TritonGPUToLLVM - pattern rewrite - register-level code - inline PTX
Step 5: LLVM backend (NVPTX/AMDGPU) - ptxas/lld - CUBIN/HSACO - driver launch
Autotuner benchmarks config variants (BLOCK, num_warps, num_stages) and caches best
Explicit data distribution is the core design - enables portable high-perf kernels
Design: higher productivity than CUDA, more flexibility than fixed libs
Tile SPMD + MLIR/LLVM - open source MIT - plugin backends
Goal: write fast custom DL primitives at tile level without hand-writing PTX/CUDA
Compiler owns layout selection, tensor core mapping, pipelining, and memory coalescing
L7 - Design Position (GPU Kernel Compiler in ML Stack)
Python tile DSL - MLIR layered IR - explicit layouts - LLVM codegen - multi-vendor backends
Init path: write @triton.jit kernel - first launch triggers compile - autotune picks config - cache binary
Step path: launch grid - driver loads CUBIN - warps execute tile program - tensor cores via MMA lowering
Sources: triton-lang.org - github.com/triton-lang/triton - PyTorch blog compilation stages - LLVM DevMtG 2024
